digest.component_or_area: BindingStore and related binding persistence subsystem
propositions: BindingStore's 799-line module conflates byte persistence, lifecycle policy, recovery, peer-state delegation, comment identity, and GET rotation without cohesive ownership, creating maintenance and regression risk.

Extraction must preserve all existing public signatures, unknown-field handling, exact JSON serialization, selective five-file publication, shallow all_bindings() behavior, and fault-cut guarantees while decomposing three internal owners: repository, lifecycle policy, and recovery.

Retirement completion uses a durable tombstone as authoritative intent; a live forward/reverse pair is removed only when tombstone, forward, and reverse identities all agree, and only explicit unretire revokes that intent.

Live recovery must run after exclusive lock/staleness validation but before remote issue fetch and binding walk, and must not interleave new liveness evidence with exact-match interrupted-retirement completion.

Production code must no longer mutate state through shallow query; lifecycle policy must expose narrow, mutation-safe seam operations while maintaining backward compatibility for all existing callers.
